observed: gst sfx-reverse tone.wav -o r.wav on a 16-bit mono 0.5 s sine: r.wav is not the exact time reversal. All 22040 non-zero samples lose 1 LSB of magnitude (positive -1, negative +1); the 10 zero samples match. Reversing r.wav again differs from the original by up to 2 LSB, so repeated passes drift.
expected: Time reversal of 16-bit PCM written back as 16-bit should be bit-exact. 24-bit and 32-bit same-width reverses should be bit-exact too.

observed: Recipe key peak_db only lowers the mix to that ceiling (tone at -6.02 dBFS stays -6.02 with peak_db -1; goes to -10.0 with peak_db -10). Upward peak normalisation needs a "normalize": true key, which neither --help nor the README names (README says only 'peak normalisation'). The shipped examples/sample-topdown/data/roar_recipe.json uses peak_db -1, which acts as a ceiling there (mix scaled -0.83 dB).
expected: --help or README should list the recipe keys (normalize, peak_db, tail_ms, layers[...]).

observed: Merging two CSVs with no collisions but keys present in only one file exits 1. --help says --no-fail covers 'collisions or missing keys' (matches behaviour); the README says the run exits 1 on collisions only.
Polarity invert went through float PCM scaled by 32767, so every non-zero 16-bit sample lost 1 LSB and a second invert drifted by up to 2. The most-negative code also failed to come back.
expected: Negating 16/24/32-bit PCM and negating again restores every sample except the most-negative code, which saturates (it has no positive twin).

observed: --swap permuted the channels and then rewrote them through the float quantizer, so a second swap was not the original file.
expected: Swapping the first two channels twice restores the PCM bytes.

observed: Splitting a stereo WAV into mono stems and joining those stems back dropped 1 LSB on the way through float PCM.
expected: Split then join, in channel order, restores the PCM bytes.

observed: --gain 0 still rewrote every non-zero sample 1 LSB quieter. 0 dB is unity.
expected: A gain of exactly 0 dB copies the PCM. Any other gain may stay on the float path.

observed: The tool says an already-mono file is copied, but the float writer dropped 1 LSB. Picking the left or right channel of a stereo file had the same loss.
expected: Already-mono, --mode left, and --mode right copy integer samples. Mixing channels is an average and stays on the float path.

observed: A reel whose peak is already under the ceiling (scale +0.00 dB) was still rewritten through float PCM, so a quiet file [0, 1, -1, 100, -100, 7] came back [0, 0, 0, 99, -99, 6].
expected: When nothing is scaled, nothing is resampled, channels are not folded, and there is no slate, the concatenated PCM matches the inputs, including exact zero gaps.

observed: --peak-db defaults to -1 and only turns a reel down. --help did not say it is a ceiling, so a quieter file looks like the flag was ignored.
expected: --help and the README should say the default -1 dBFS value is a ceiling.

observed: tone.wav reports DC [0.0] -> [0.0] but the written file differed in every non-zero sample, because a zero subtraction still went through the float writer.
expected: When each channel mean rounds to 0, the output PCM matches the input. A real offset is subtracted as a whole number of samples.

observed: anim-from-folder and anim-meta write {"clips": {"walk": {...}}}. anim-retarget-fps exited 1 with 'no clips/animations array found' on that file. It only accepted a list.
expected: The name-keyed clips object is retargeted and written back as an object, with each clip's fps updated.
